content: Cimetidine has the potential to increase the risk of adverse reactions associated with substrates of the Breast Cancer Resistance Protein (BCRP). Adjustments to the dosages of other BCRP substrates may be necessary, and close monitoring is advised. Cimetidine increases the plasma levels and effects of morphine by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. This interaction is significant, and alternative medications should be considered. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine enhances the effects of nalbuphine by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative medications should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of nateglinide by interfering with its metabolism via the hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of nebivolol by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine elevates the levels or effects of nelfinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative medications should be used due to the seriousness of this interaction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine also increases nelfinavir levels by affecting its metabolism via the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of neratinib by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine raises the levels of inhaled nicotine by reducing renal clearance. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Cimetidine increases the levels of intranasal nicotine by both decreasing its metabolism and reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine elevates the levels or effects of nifedipine by interfering with its metabolism via the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine reduces the levels of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Cimetidine increases nilotinib levels by affecting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of nimodipine by inhibiting its metabolism via the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by both inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 and raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine elevates the levels or effects of nortriptyline by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of olanzapine by interfering with its metabolism via the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. Cimetidine enhances the effects of opium tincture by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine increases the levels of ospemifene by interfering with its metabolism via the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. Cimetidine increases its own levels when coadministered with oteseconazole, likely due to other mechanisms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Oteseconazole, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the effects and toxicity risks of BCRP substrates. Use the lowest starting dose of the BCRP substrate or consider reducing its dose. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of oxybutynin by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of oxycodone by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine elevates the levels or effects of oxymorphone by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of paclitaxel by interfering with its metabolism via the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine enhances the effects of papaveretum by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of parecoxib by interfering with its metabolism via the hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 and the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of paroxetine by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine reduces the levels or effects of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of pazopanib with drugs that raise gastric pH; consider short-acting antacids instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and H2 antagonists, and separate antacid and pazopanib dosing by several hours. Cimetidine increases the levels of pefloxacin by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. Cimetidine enhances the effects of pentazocine by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of phenytoin by interfering with its metabolism via the hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of pramipexole by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine elevates the levels or effects of praziquantel by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 and the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of propranolol by interfering with its metabolism via the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine elevates the levels or effects of quinidine by interfering with its metabolism via the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of quinine by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug and by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of rabeprazole by interfering with its metabolism via the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2, the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, and the hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. Cimetidine elevates the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of rasagiline by interfering with its metabolism via the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. Use caution and monitor closely. Limit the rasagiline dose to 5 mg daily when combined with CYP1A2 inhibitors. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of regorafenib by other mechanisms, likely involving BCRP (ABCG2) transport inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Coadministration with a BCRP substrate may increase systemic exposure to the substrate and related toxicity. Cimetidine raises the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cimetidine reduces the levels or effects of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Concurrent use may lead to treatment failure and/or the development of rilpivirine or NNRTI resistance due to decreased levels. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of risedronate by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
